verdict.line: You lose if you trade into her Q cone or get caught by an E all-in before level 6; you win if you survive lane, stack Q, and hit your Trinity Force/Frozen Heart timing.

brief.thesis: Gwen's whole pattern runs through E (Skip 'n Slash) to engage and Hallowed Mist (W) to disengage safely, while A Thousand Cuts punishes exactly the max-health stat Nasus stacks. You have no ranged answer to her 450-range Q cone and no dash to punish her E, so you lose straight trades until Wither and raw Q stacks catch up. It's a Gwen-favored lane in a vacuum (45.1% win rate over 91 games), but Nasus's scaling through Q kills and his item timings give him a real path back if he doesn't feed a solo kill early.

theirWindow.when: Her E and Q are both up
theirWindow.what: She dashes in with E (Skip 'n Slash), lands the true-damage center hit of Q (Snip Snip!) and autos for A Thousand Cuts procs, then dashes out and partially refreshes E if it connects. Back off and take the chip damage rather than standing in the cone to trade.

yourWindow.when: Her E (Skip 'n Slash) is on cooldown
yourWindow.what: At that point she has no dash for 11-13s depending on rank, so she can't cleanly engage or escape. Step up, land Q and autos, and fire Wither the moment she tries to walk away to kill her attack and move speed.

start.why: You need the flat damage reduction and sustain to survive her Q poke and A Thousand Cuts procs through level 5, since you can't out-range or out-trade her yet.

boots.why: Lower cooldowns on Siphoning Strike and Wither let you re-apply the slow and stack Q faster, which matters more here than magic resist since you have no gap closer to force fights anyway.

core.why: The spellblade proc and stat spike give you the burst to actually punish her when her E is down, matching both measured build paths.
The attack speed reduction directly cuts her A Thousand Cuts proc rate in extended trades, and this order has the higher recorded win rate (62.5% over 8 games) of the two paths.
Magic resist and heal amp counter her magic-heavy on-hit damage and boost Soul Eater lifesteal in skirmishes.

situational.when: she keeps healing back up through A Thousand Cuts in extended trades
her Needlework (R) stacks are deleting you in skirmishes and you need tenacity and magic resist
you're ahead and want faster cooldowns to chain Q kills and all-ins

runes.keystoneWhy: The healing and movement speed on landing Q offsets her poke since she has no hard engage to punish the speed boost, keeping you alive long enough to stack Q.

summoners.why: This combo has the best recorded win rate (46.8%) and highest pick rate (43.5%) in this matchup. Teleport lets you reset after losing early trades or impact a sidelane since you have no gap closer, and Ghost closes distance in skirmishes where her E dash would otherwise out-rotate you.

playing.title: Farm under tower early
playing.detail: Before level 6, prioritize Q last-hits over melee trades; her Q cone and A Thousand Cuts win straight exchanges.

playing.title: Punish her E cooldown
playing.detail: When Skip 'n Slash is down for 11-13s, she has no dash to engage or escape; step up and force a trade with Q and autos.

playing.title: Don't walk into Hallowed Mist
playing.detail: Inside the mist she can be targeted but is also protected from anyone outside it; stay outside, farm, and let the mist expire instead of diving it.

playing.title: Time Wither on her commit
playing.detail: Fire Wither the instant she uses E or Q to engage, slowing her move and attack speed before she can kite or disengage.

playing.title: Stack Q on minions
playing.detail: Siphoning Strike drops to a 4s cooldown at rank 5; kill as many minions with it as possible since the bonus damage snowballs your late game.

playing.title: Avoid solo kills before 6
playing.detail: She has the measured solo-kill edge pre-Fury of the Sands; don't start extended skirmishes until your R is live.

playing.title: All-in after Frozen Heart
playing.detail: Once Frozen Heart's attack speed slow is online, her A Thousand Cuts proc rate drops sharply; look for all-ins in that item window with R up.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, rune, summoner, and win-rate numbers are measured from real games on the current patch (16.20.1); the mechanical reasoning and trade-pattern advice are my own tactical read, not measured data.
